# HLogViewer

> A bounded log tail with search, level filtering, pause/follow controls, and copy support.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HLogViewer` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-log-viewer>`.
- Constructor: `HearthLogViewerElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Surfaces.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HLogViewer.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The component renders a bounded tail (500 entries by default), filters that tail, and follows new entries while follow is enabled. It does not fetch or stream logs.
- Scrolling away from the bottom pauses following. Log content is escaped and not continuously announced as a live region.
- Use server-paged/virtualized history for large archives. Copy includes only currently visible/filtered entries.

## Public API

entries: LogEntry[] · label: string · follow, wrap: boolean · maxLines: number = 500

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    entries: LogEntry[];
    label?: string;
    follow?: boolean;
    maxLines?: number;
    wrap?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ entries: () => [], label: "Logs", follow: true, maxLines: 500 }
```

### Events

update:follow(boolean), search-change(query), copied(), copy-error(message)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:follow": [
        follow: boolean
    ];
    "search-change": [
        query: string
    ];
    copied: [
    ];
    "copy-error": [
        message: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, header, viewport, line

Use `hearth-log-viewer::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface LogEntry {
    id: string;
    message: string;
    timestamp?: string;
    level?: "debug" | "info" | "warning" | "error";
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HLogViewer } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const entries = [{id:'1',timestamp:'12:00:00',level:'info' as const,message:'Provider connected.'},{id:'2',timestamp:'12:00:01',level:'warning' as const,message:'One route is unresolved.'}];
</script>

<template>
  <HLogViewer :entries="entries" label="Provider logs" :max-lines="500" wrap />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-log-viewer');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Provider logs",
  "maxLines": 500,
  "wrap": true,
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "timestamp": "12:00:00",
      "level": "info",
      "message": "Provider connected."
    }
  ]
});

mount.append(element);
```
